pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


Have you ever watched a movie that starts with a rescue? Maybe a firefighter runs into a burning building. Maybe a lifeguard dives into the water. Maybe a soldier carries a wounded friend to safety. You see the rescue. You feel the tension. You cheer for the hero. But you might not understand why the rescue was needed. You might not understand the backstory. You might not understand the plan.


The Bible starts with a rescue. It starts with a hero. It starts with a plan. The book of Genesis is not just a book of beginnings. It is a book of rescue. It is the beginning of the rescue. It tells us why we need to be rescued. It tells us who is going to rescue us. It tells us how the rescue will happen. And every story in Genesis points to the rescue. Every story points to Jesus.


This book is for the curious. It is for the spiritual seeker who wants to understand the rescue. It is for the person who wants to see the plan. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 stories from Genesis. We are going to see the rescue. We are going to see the hero. And we are going to see Jesus.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see Genesis as a collection of old stories. You will see it as a rescue plan. You will see it as a preparation. You will see it as a promise. You will understand the beginning of the rescue. You will understand why you need to be rescued. You will understand who rescues you. You will have a new confidence in your faith. You will have a new love for your Bible. And you will have a new appreciation for the hero of the rescue.


How to Use This Guide

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever started a book and known the ending? Maybe you read the last page first. Maybe someone spoiled it for you. Maybe you watched the movie. You know how it ends. But you still read the book. You still watch the movie. You still want to see how they get there. The Bible is like that. We know the ending. We know Jesus wins. But we still read the beginning. We still want to see how the rescue begins. And it begins in Genesis.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth." - Genesis 1:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


This is the first verse in the Bible. It is the beginning. It is the start. It is the opening scene. God created everything. He created the heavens. He created the earth. He created the stage. He created the setting. He created the world where the rescue would happen.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." - John 1:1


The Gospel of John opens with the same words. "In the beginning." But John reveals the Word. The Word was with God. The Word was God. The Word is Jesus. Jesus was there in the beginning. He was there when the rescue began.


The Verdict
The rescue begins with creation. Jesus is the creator. The pattern is exact. The plan is precise. The rescue is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you ever feel like your life is just a random story? Do you ever feel like there is no plan? Remember the beginning. Remember the rescue. God created everything with a plan. He created you with a plan. You are part of the rescue story.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the beginning. Thank you for the rescue. Thank you for the plan. Thank you for Jesus. Help me to see my part in the rescue story. Help me to trust your plan. Help me to follow the hero. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever watched a movie without a villain? It is boring. There is no conflict. There is no tension. There is no rescue. A rescue needs a villain. A rescue needs an enemy. A rescue needs a bad guy. The Bible has a villain. It has an enemy. It has a bad guy. And the rescue begins with the villain.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Now the serpent was more crafty than any of the wild animals the LORD God had made." - Genesis 3:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The serpent enters the story. He is crafty. He is sneaky. He is deceptive. He is the villain. He is the enemy. He is the bad guy. He questions God. He tempts Eve. He brings sin into the world. He is the reason we need a rescue.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The great dragon was hurled down—that ancient serpent called the devil, or Satan, who leads the whole world astray." - Revelation 12:9


The serpent is the devil. He is Satan. He is the ancient serpent. He is the villain. But Jesus defeats him. Jesus crushes his head. Jesus wins the victory. The rescue is possible because the hero defeats the villain.


The Verdict
The rescue needs a villain. The villain is the serpent. The hero is Jesus. The pattern is exact. The plan is precise. The rescue is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like there is a villain in your story? Do you feel like there is an enemy? Do you feel like there is a bad guy? Remember the rescue. Remember the hero. Jesus defeats the villain. Jesus crushes the serpent. You are on the winning side.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for defeating the villain. Thank you for crushing the serpent. Thank you for winning the victory. Help me to trust your victory. Help me to live in your victory. Help me to resist the enemy. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever watched a movie without a problem? It is boring. There is no tension. There is no conflict. There is no rescue. A rescue needs a problem. A rescue needs a crisis. A rescue needs a need. The Bible has a problem. It has a crisis. It has a need. And the rescue begins with the problem.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"When the woman saw that the fruit of the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eye, and also desirable for gaining wisdom, she took some and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it." - Genesis 3:6 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


The problem is sin. The problem is disobedience. The problem is rebellion. Adam and Eve ate the fruit. They disobeyed God. They chose their own way. They brought sin into the world. They brought death into the world. They brought separation into the world. They created the problem that needs to be rescued.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous." - Romans 5:19


The problem is sin. But the solution is Jesus. Jesus obeyed. Jesus kept the command. Jesus brought righteousness. Jesus solved the problem. The rescue is possible because the hero solves the problem.


The Verdict
The rescue needs a problem. The problem is sin. The solution is Jesus. The pattern is exact. The plan is precise. The rescue is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like your life is a problem? Do you feel like you are a problem? Do you feel like you cannot fix yourself? Remember the rescue. Remember the solution. Jesus solves the problem. Jesus fixes the broken. Jesus saves the lost.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for solving the problem. Thank you for fixing the broken. Thank you for saving the lost. Help me to trust your solution. Help me to live in your righteousness. Help me to rest in your obedience. Amen.

The Prayer

The Hook
Have you ever watched a movie without a covering? It is uncomfortable. There is shame. There is guilt. There is nakedness. A rescue needs a covering. A rescue needs a garment. A rescue needs a gift. The Bible has a covering. It has a garment. It has a gift. And the rescue begins with the covering.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them." - Genesis 3:21 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


God made garments of skin. He made clothes. He made a covering. An animal had to die. Blood had to be shed. It was a sacrifice. It was a gift. It was a covering for their shame. It was a covering for their sin.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ." - Galatians 3:27


Jesus is the covering. He is the garment. He is the gift. His blood was shed. His life was given. He covers our shame. He covers our sin. He covers our nakedness.


The Verdict
The rescue needs a covering. The covering is Jesus. The pattern is exact. The plan is precise. The rescue is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you need a covering? Do you need a garment? Do you need a gift? Remember the covering. Remember Jesus. He is the covering. He is the garment. He is the gift. He covers your shame. He covers your sin.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the covering. Thank you for the garment. Thank you for the gift. Thank you for shedding your blood. Thank you for giving your life. Help me to wear your covering. Help me to rest in your sacrifice. Amen.

The Ancient Text (OT)

The Verdict

The Resonance

The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the walk. Thank you for the journey. Thank you for the path. Thank you for walking with me. Thank you for seeking me. Thank you for saving me. Help me to walk with you. Help me to follow the path. Amen.

pages.title: Day 29: The Rescue Needs a Promise

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever watched a movie and finally understood the rescue? Maybe you saw the hero save the day. Maybe you saw the plan come together. Maybe you saw the ending. The Bible is like that. We see the rescue. We see the hero. We see the ending. And the rescue is Jesus. The hero is Jesus. The ending is Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel." - Genesis 3:15 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


This is the first promise. This is the first gospel. This is the first rescue. God promised a hero. God promised a deliverer. God promised a rescuer. And the rescue is Jesus.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


Jesus is the rescue. He is the hero. He is the deliverer. He is the rescuer. He crushed the serpent's head. He defeated the devil. He saved the world. The rescue is Jesus.


The Verdict
The rescue is Jesus. The pattern is exact. The plan is precise. The rescue is Jesus.


The Resonance
You have seen the rescue. You have seen the hero. You have seen the ending. The rescue is Jesus. Now what? You can trust the rescue. You can trust the hero. You can trust Jesus.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the rescue. Thank you for being the hero. Thank you for being the deliverer. Thank you for being the rescuer. Help me to trust the rescue. Help me to trust the hero. Help me to trust you. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Rescue Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 stories in Genesis. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of Luke. It is 24 chapters. It is the perfect follow-up to this book. It tells the story of the rescue. It tells the story of Jesus. As you read, look for the rescue. Look for the hero. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The stories are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The stories point to a person. The stories point to Jesus. You can understand the stories and still miss the rescue. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The stories are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.


Coming Next: The Seed of the Woman
If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. The Seed of the Woman takes a 30 day look at the ancient prophecy hidden in the garden. It is for the seeker who wants to go further.


Final Call to Action
Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of seekers. The investigation is not over. The adventure is just beginning.

A dark, midnight blue background. A glowing, ancient scroll unrolls across the cover. On the scroll, a blueprint of a rescue is drawn in silver lines. A hero is reaching down to save a fallen figure. The title THE BEGINNING OF THE RESCUE is in a bold, modern, metallic white font. The subtitle is in a clean, elegant serif font. The overall feel is mysterious, authoritative, and intellectually premium.
